In FirstOrder/Arithmetic/HFS/Basic.lean, there are some definability instances named union_definable, product_definable, domain_definable, etc.

In FirstOrder/SetTheory/Z.lean, there are some definability instances named union.definable, prod.definable, etc. Similarly, in FirstOrder/SetTheory/Function.lean, there are domain.definable, function.definable, etc.

I have been thinking about renaming these to make their naming conventions match. Should I do this, and if I should, should I rename the arithmetic instances or the set theory instances?

To be honest, I’m also undecided about which notation to officially adopt. The union_definable-style is correct in terms of naming conventions, but I think union.definable easier to understand.

A similar issue exists with the naming conventions for functions and relations in the model and the semisentences that define them. For relations, it seems best to use uppercase Relation for the model and lowercase relation for the corresponding semisentence, but this approach doesn’t work the same way for functions. I’m currently using notations like Function and function.dfn, but this is not looks good.

Anyway, for now, I think we should follow the conventions of SetTheory.
Thanks! Since you're undecided I will not update this now.
